internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 3 occurrences the root marks something that has gone far beyond the proper bound. In 18:14 and 72:4 it is a statement (object of a speech verb) that overshoots the truth about God — an extreme, far-fetched falsehood. In 38:22 it is a verb (Form IV) asking a judge not to overshoot the standard of just judgment ("judge with truth and do not shaṭaṭ"). Speech-excess vs. judicial-excess are different domains, but the same core "far past the correct limit" is present in each.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: N (شَطَطًا, the excess-thing itself, 18:14 & 72:4) vs. V(IV) (تُشْطِط, the act of pushing oneself beyond the bound, 38:22) — the IV form supplies the causative/agentive "act to excess," which is subtracted. CONSTRUCTION: in both N cases شَطَطًا is the accusative object of a verb of saying (قُلْنَا / يَقُولُ), i.e. a statement characterized as overshooting; in 38:22 it is a prohibitive imperative on the judge. CONTEXT: theological speech (18:14, 72:4) vs. judicial conduct (38:22). After subtracting form (thing vs. act), construction (spoken object vs. prohibition), and context (theology vs. court), the residue "remote overshoot of the correct limit" remains in all three.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 38:22 (تُشْطِط) is the hardest: read loosely it could mean simply "be unjust," collapsing the root into ظلم/جور and losing distinctiveness. But its pairing with "احكم بالحق" (judge with the truth) frames it as overshooting/deviating far from the truth-standard, preserving the "far beyond the mark" residue rather than a generic "do wrong." It reconciles.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: That the contribution is generic "injustice/wrongdoing/falsehood" (≈ ظلم / جور / بغى). This is weaker: it fails to explain the distinctive distance/farness component, and it would make شطط redundant with بغى, which occurs in the very same verse (38:22) yet is contrasted with it. The "remote overshoot" reading uniquely unifies both an extreme false statement (far from truth) and excessive judgment (far from fair) under one spatial-excess metaphor.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct from بغى (aggression/transgression against a party — co-occurs in 38:22 and is contrasted), from ظلم (wrongdoing in general), from جور (deviation from straightness), and from إسراف (wasteful excess). شطط specifically encodes the remoteness/farness of the overshoot from the correct bound. The in-verse contrast with بغى at 38:22 is direct falsifiable evidence for the distinction.
